cross_references.description: Accident date March 24, 2019 confirmed across airframe examination, site onscene, meteorology report, GPS report, party representatives statement, and both toxicology reports
Aircraft type Cessna 172M confirmed by airframe examination, site onscene, meteorology report, GPS report, and ATC transcript
Aircraft serial number 1726139 confirmed by both airframe examination and site onscene information
Accident time approximately 1815 PST corroborated by GPS specialist report, meteorology report, and site onscene information
Aircraft registration N-XXXX corroborated across airframe examination, site onscene, and meteorology report
Pilot-1 holds commercial pilot certificate confirmed by GPS report, meteorology report, and site onscene information
Fatal injuries to Pilot-1 and Passenger-1 corroborated by GPS report, meteorology report, and site onscene information
Flight operated under 14 CFR Part 91 personal flight confirmed by GPS report, meteorology report, and site onscene information
Meteorological conditions described as undetermined night meteorological conditions in both GPS specialist report and site onscene information
No evidence of pre-impact mechanical malfunction or structural failure corroborated by airframe examination and site onscene information
No evidence of in-flight or post-impact fire confirmed by airframe examination and site onscene information
Both fuel caps found securely fastened corroborated by airframe examination (at facility) and site onscene information
Propeller fracture-separated from engine/crankshaft flange confirmed by both airframe examination and site onscene information
Propeller described as metal two-bladed fixed-pitch in both airframe examination and site onscene information
N-XXXX contact at 0144 UTC with SOCAL Approach/POMR reported identically in ATC transcript and FAA communications summary
N-XXXX contact with SPG sector at 0207 UTC at 3500 ft reported in both ATC transcript and FAA communications summary
N-XXXX position report 4 nm east of Airport-India above windmill at ~0208 UTC recorded identically in ATC transcript and FAA communications summary
SPG radar contact 7 miles east of Airport-India at 0211 UTC with altimeter 29.80 documented in both ATC transcript and FAA communications summary
Loss of radar contact at 0216 UTC and termination of flight following documented in both ATC transcript and FAA communications summary
HEM controller advisory about C-17 heavy climbing to 5000 ft turning southwest at 0148 UTC recorded in both ATC transcript and FAA communications summary
N-XXXX departure from Airport-Charlie at approximately 1530-1540 PST on March 24 corroborated by dispatch email and Witness-3 testimony

Causal chain: pilot not endorsed for night flying (pilot_rental_privileges), yet reservation extended past sunset (dispatch_sheet), and CFI-1 warned of dangerous mountain pass winds (witness_testimony_04) - all contributing to fatal outcome
Causal chain: pilot flew consistently at 3500 ft (ATC/site), accident site at ~2465-2500 ft MSL (site/meteorology), inadequate terrain clearance at night with poor visibility
Pilot-1's last fueling of N-XXXX (12.5 gallons on March 22) and no activity before accident corroborated across dispatch email and fueling procedures documents
Causal chain: no standard weather briefing found (meteorology report), operator procedure requires briefing via 1-800-992-7433 prior to any flight (operator_procedures)
